sections.markdown:
## C — Light, weather and driving emergencies
FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A01
Night driving combines reduced visibility, oncoming glare, crossing animals and eyestrain, requiring greater alertness. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A01
Headlights are required from one-half hour after sunset through one-half hour before sunrise. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A01
Headlights are also required when low light or adverse weather prevents clearly seeing people and vehicles 1,000 feet ahead. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A01
Turn on low beams as daylight fades so other drivers can identify the vehicle and its actions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A01
Parking lights alone are not lawful when headlights are required. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A01
Increase following space when you cannot see clearly. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A01
In the handbook's night-driving illustration, traveling above 55 mph exceeds the distance illuminated far enough ahead for a stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A02
Use high beams on rural highways and low beams when following, meeting oncoming traffic or driving in town. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A02
Dim headlights at least 500 feet before meeting another vehicle; the handbook describes that as about four to five seconds. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A02
When approaching within 300 feet behind another vehicle, dim headlights to the lowest beam. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A02
Low beams must be aimed to avoid glare at all times. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A02
Clean both sides of the windshield to reduce glare from oncoming vehicles. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A02
Clean headlights improve the light available for seeing ahead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A02
Keep the eyes moving rather than staring at the headlight spot, which can contribute to eyestrain, fatigue and poor concentration. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A02
At night, scan for animals, pedestrians and bicycles and look sideways for lights from vehicles entering or crossing ahead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A02
Check the lights of vehicles ahead for signs of speed or lane-position changes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A02
Use low-beam headlights in fog; front fog lights may sometimes help. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A02
Use red rear fog lights only in heavy fog or similar hazardous weather that seriously reduces visibility. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A02
Switch rear fog lights off once visibility improves. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A02
Reduce normal speed in fog while watching the difference from surrounding traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F21 | anchor: A02
The fog discussion warns of high crash risk when speed differs from other traffic by more than 15 mph. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

sections.domain: Light, weather and driving emergencies — C.02
sections.heading: C — Light, weather and driving emergencies
sections.markdown:
## C — Light, weather and driving emergencies
FACT_ID: sec13-F22 | anchor: A02
Stop at the nearest safe location if fog could create a large speed difference from other traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F23 | anchor: A02
If fog prevents seeing at least 10 seconds ahead, consider pulling off at the nearest safe place and stopping. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F24 | anchor: A03
In poor visibility, scan for vehicle lights, pedestrians and stopped or slow vehicles while enlarging the space cushion as much as possible. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F25 | anchor: A03
Slow down on slippery pavement because stopping distance increases. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F26 | anchor: A03
In rain, double a car's following interval to four seconds. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F27 | anchor: A03
Use low-beam headlights during rain. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F28 | anchor: A03
Replace wiper blades if they smear or streak the windshield. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F29 | anchor: A03
Use extra care during the first half hour of rain, when dust and oil mix with water and make the road slippery. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F30 | anchor: A03
Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on a thin water film rather than the pavement. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F31 | anchor: A03
Slowing down helps prevent hydroplaning during rain. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F32 | anchor: A03
The snow-and-ice guidance recommends snow tires or chains to resist skidding and reduce stopping distance. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F33 | anchor: A03
On snow or ice, avoid sudden speed or direction changes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F34 | anchor: A03
Watch for ice on bridges and shaded road areas. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F35 | anchor: A03
For snow, the source triples a car's forward cushion to six seconds. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F36 | anchor: A03
For ice, the source quadruples a car's forward cushion to eight seconds. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F37 | anchor: A03
Keep vehicle windows clear to see and communicate with other road users. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F38 | anchor: A03
On snow or ice, slow gradually and smoothly before stopping or turning. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F39 | anchor: A03
Avoid locking the wheels because steering control depends on their rotation. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F40 | anchor: A03
Do not use cruise control on snow or ice. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F41 | anchor: A03
Wind is particularly hazardous for trucks, recreational vehicles, campers and trailer-towing drivers, and lower speed is the source's recommended defense. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

Misconceptions: Pumping conventional brakes and holding steady ABS pressure are different instructions; emergency acceleration is discussed only for a side or rear threat when room exists.
Mnemonics: Recall index: condition, braking system, space, controlled response; this organizer adds no emergency maneuver to the source.
Glossary: Recall terms: low beam, rear fog light, hydroplaning, ABS, blowout, steering lock and shoulder.
Dynamic facts: Vehicle-specific procedures, equipment capabilities and present legal applicability remain edition-bound. No old ignition-system table is generalized to modern vehicles.
